name: Reckoner
text: A block that runs a Lua program. Use a book and quill (or a written book) on it to load the program from its pages, then use it bare-handed, or give it a rising redstone signal, to run it; use it again to stop a running program. Programs can print, sleep(ticks), read redstone from each side, set the redstone it gives out, list the items in a neighbouring chest, write to a sign beside it with monitor.write(side, line, text), and send and receive wireless messages within 64 blocks with net.listen, net.send, net.receive and net.wait; with Cable blocks touching both computers, messages travel at any distance. monitor.write also drives a stack of up to eight signs hung below the first (32 rows), monitor.clear(side) blanks it and monitor.rows(side) counts rows. A Disk Drive beside it holds a Disk: disk.present, list, read, write, delete, free (16 files, 8000 characters each, 32000 in all). A slice of a program that runs past 200,000 instructions is stopped. Age VI.

name: Wayfarer
text: A Reckoner that walks. It moves one block at a time, digs, places blocks, drops and picks up items and carries sixteen stacks. drop and suck move items into and out of a chest or other container in front of it. It burns fuel to move: turtle.refuel() burns a fuel item from the selected slot (a second of burn time is one unit; it starts with 20). turtle.forward(), back(), up(), down(), turnLeft(), turnRight(), dig(dir), place(dir), detect(dir), inspect(dir), drop(dir), suck(dir), select(n), getCount(n), getItem(n), getFuel(); directions are forward, back, left, right, up, down. Loaded and started like a Reckoner, and it has the same net, monitor, redstone and sleep functions. Age VII.

name: Cable
text: A thin run of metal that joins Reckoners and Wayfarers into one wired network. A message sent by a computer touching a connected run of cable (up to 512 cables) reaches every listening computer touching it, at any distance. Age VI.

name: Disk Drive
text: Holds one Disk beside a Reckoner or Wayfarer. Use a Disk on it to put it in; sneak with an empty hand to take it out. Programs use disk.present, list, read, write, delete and free on the side it sits. A disk keeps 16 files of up to 8000 characters, 32000 in all. Age VI.

name: Disk
text: A small card of files for a Disk Drive. Carries its files wherever it goes. Age VI.
